           1 +"""Client for the black-box environment server.
           2 +
           3 +This file is copied into the agent sandbox. Import it in test and
           4 +exploration scripts to interact with the environment without access to its
           5 +source code::
           6 +
           7 +    from env_client import make_env
           8 +
           9 +    env = make_env()
          10 +    obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)
          11 +    obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
          12 +    state = env.get_state()
          13 +    env.set_state(state)
          14 +    primitives = env.make_primitives()  # same dict the eval harness passes
          15 +    env.close()
          16 +
          17 +Each call to ``make_env()`` creates a fresh, independent environment
          18 +instance on the server, so parallel test scripts are safe.
          19 +
          20 +The list above is the legacy blackbox interface. When ``env_spaces.json`` has
          21 +``"strict": true``, only reset, step, rendering, close, and generic space metadata
          22 +are supported; the host server rejects every other helper command independently.
          23 +
          24 +NOTE: ``approach.py`` must NOT import this module. It is evaluated by a
          25 +separate harness that calls it directly with real observations; this client
          26 +is only for test and exploration scripts.
          27 +
          28 +This module must stay importable with only the standard library and numpy.
          29 +"""
          30 +
          31 +from __future__ import annotations
          32 +
          33 +import importlib
          34 +import json
          35 +import socket
          36 +import sys
          37 +from pathlib import Path
          38 +from typing import Any
          39 +
          40 +import numpy as np
          41 +
          42 +_METADATA_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "env_spaces.json"
          43 +_NDARRAY_TAG = "__ndarray__"
          44 +_HANDLE_TAG = "__handle__"
          45 +_MODULE_TAG = "__module__"
          46 +_SET_TAG = "__set__"
          47 +_OCS_TAG = "__ocs__"
          48 +
          49 +
          50 +# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
          51 +# Local ObjectCentricState mirror
          52 +#
          53 +# A variable-count env hands the program an ObjectCentricState. This sandbox module
          54 +# must stay importable with only the standard library and numpy, so rather than import
          55 +# relational_structs it reconstructs a faithful local mirror from the self-contained
          56 +# codec payload (which embeds the type hierarchy). The mirror implements the subset of
          57 +# the ObjectCentricState API a generated program uses, with the same semantics -- most
          58 +# importantly `is_instance` over the ancestor chain and `get(obj, feature)` by name --
          59 +# so a program tested here behaves as it will at eval against the real state.
          60 +# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
          61 +
          62 +
          63 +class _Type:
          64 +    """A local mirror of relational_structs.Type (name + optional parent)."""
          65 +
          66 +    def __init__(self, name: str, parent: "_Type | None" = None) -> None:
          67 +        self.name = name
          68 +        self.parent = parent
          69 +
          70 +    def get_ancestors(self) -> set["_Type"]:
          71 +        """Return this type and all of its ancestors (parents, grandparents, ...)."""
          72 +        ancestors: set[_Type] = set()
          73 +        cur: _Type | None = self
          74 +        while cur is not None:
          75 +            ancestors.add(cur)
          76 +            cur = cur.parent
          77 +        return ancestors
          78 +
          79 +    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
          80 +        return isinstance(other, _Type) and other.name == self.name
          81 +
          82 +    def __hash__(self) -> int:
          83 +        return hash(self.name)
          84 +
          85 +    def __repr__(self) -> str:
          86 +        # Match relational_structs.Type's dataclass repr, including name quoting.
          87 +        # Policies must see the same strings during synthesis and evaluation.
          88 +        return f"Type(name={self.name!r})"
          89 +
          90 +
          91 +class _Object:
          92 +    """A local mirror of relational_structs.Object (name + type)."""
          93 +
          94 +    def __init__(self, name: str, typ: _Type) -> None:
          95 +        self.name = name
          96 +        self.type = typ
          97 +
          98 +    def is_instance(self, typ: _Type) -> bool:
          99 +        """True if this object's type is *typ* or a descendant of it."""
         100 +        return typ in self.type.get_ancestors()
         101 +
         102 +    def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
         103 +        return isinstance(other, _Object) and other.name == self.name
         104 +
         105 +    def __hash__(self) -> int:
         106 +        return hash(self.name)
         107 +
         108 +    def __repr__(self) -> str:
         109 +        return f"{self.name}:{self.type.name}"
         110 +
         111 +
         112 +class _ObjectCentricState:
         113 +    """A local mirror of relational_structs.ObjectCentricState.
         114 +
         115 +    Holds ``{Object: feature ndarray}`` as ``data`` plus ``{Type: [feature names]}`` as
         116 +    ``type_features`` (both public, matching the real state) and exposes the read/write
         117 +    API a program uses. Iteration yields the objects, sorted by name for determinism.
         118 +    """
         119 +
         120 +    def __init__(
         121 +        self,
         122 +        data: dict[_Object, np.ndarray],
         123 +        type_features: dict[_Type, list[str]],
         124 +    ) -> None:
         125 +        self.data = data
         126 +        self.type_features = type_features
         127 +
         128 +    def __iter__(self) -> Any:
         129 +        return iter(sorted(self.data, key=lambda o: o.name))
         130 +
         131 +    def get_object_names(self) -> set[str]:
         132 +        """The set of object names in this state."""
         133 +        return {o.name for o in self.data}
         134 +
         135 +    def get_object_from_name(self, name: str) -> _Object:
         136 +        """The object with the given name."""
         137 +        for obj in self.data:
         138 +            if obj.name == name:
         139 +                return obj
         140 +        raise ValueError(f"No object named {name!r}")
         141 +
         142 +    def get_objects(self, typ: _Type) -> list[_Object]:
         143 +        """Objects that are instances of *typ* (its subtypes included), by name."""
         144 +        return sorted(
         145 +            (o for o in self.data if o.is_instance(typ)), key=lambda o: o.name
         146 +        )
         147 +
         148 +    def _feature_index(self, obj: _Object, feature: str) -> int:
         149 +        return self.type_features[obj.type].index(feature)
         150 +
         151 +    def get(self, obj: _Object, feature: str) -> float:
         152 +        """Read a named feature of an object."""
         153 +        return float(self.data[obj][self._feature_index(obj, feature)])
         154 +
         155 +    def set(self, obj: _Object, feature: str, value: float) -> None:
         156 +        """Write a named feature of an object in place."""
         157 +        self.data[obj][self._feature_index(obj, feature)] = value
         158 +
         159 +    def vec(self, objects: Any) -> np.ndarray:
         160 +        """Concatenate the feature vectors of the given objects."""
         161 +        return (
         162 +            np.concatenate([self.data[o] for o in objects]) if objects else np.array([])
         163 +        )
         164 +
         165 +    def copy(self) -> "_ObjectCentricState":
         166 +        """A deep copy of this state."""
         167 +        return _ObjectCentricState(
         168 +            {o: arr.copy() for o, arr in self.data.items()},
         169 +            {t: list(f) for t, f in self.type_features.items()},
         170 +        )
         171 +
         172 +    def allclose(self, other: "_ObjectCentricState") -> bool:
         173 +        """True if *other* has the same objects with numerically-close features."""
         174 +        if self.get_object_names() != other.get_object_names():
         175 +            return False
         176 +        return all(
         177 +            np.allclose(self.data[o], other.data[other.get_object_from_name(o.name)])
         178 +            for o in self.data
         179 +        )
         180 +
         181 +
         182 +def _build_local_types(
         183 +    types_payload: list[dict[str, Any]],
         184 +) -> tuple[dict[str, _Type], dict[_Type, list[str]]]:
         185 +    """Rebuild local {name: _Type} and {_Type: [features]} (parents-first payload)."""
         186 +    type_by_name: dict[str, _Type] = {}
         187 +    type_features: dict[_Type, list[str]] = {}
         188 +    for entry in types_payload:
         189 +        parent = type_by_name[entry["parent"]] if entry["parent"] is not None else None
         190 +        typ = _Type(entry["name"], parent)
         191 +        type_by_name[entry["name"]] = typ
         192 +        type_features[typ] = list(entry["features"])
         193 +    return type_by_name, type_features
         194 +
         195 +
         196 +def _ocs_from_payload(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> _ObjectCentricState:
         197 +    """Reconstruct a local ObjectCentricState from a self-contained codec payload."""
         198 +    type_by_name, type_features = _build_local_types(payload["types"])
         199 +    data: dict[_Object, np.ndarray] = {}
         200 +    for entry in payload["objects"]:
         201 +        obj = _Object(entry["name"], type_by_name[entry["type"]])
         202 +        data[obj] = np.array(entry["features"], dtype=np.float32)
         203 +    return _ObjectCentricState(data, type_features)
         204 +
         205 +
         206 +def _ocs_to_payload(state: _ObjectCentricState) -> dict[str, Any]:
         207 +    """Encode a local ObjectCentricState back to the self-contained codec payload."""
         208 +
         209 +    def depth(t: _Type) -> int:
         210 +        n, p = 0, t.parent
         211 +        while p is not None:
         212 +            n, p = n + 1, p.parent
         213 +        return n
         214 +
         215 +    types = sorted(state.type_features, key=lambda t: (depth(t), t.name))
         216 +    return {
         217 +        "types": [
         218 +            {
         219 +                "name": t.name,
         220 +                "parent": t.parent.name if t.parent is not None else None,
         221 +                "features": list(state.type_features[t]),
         222 +            }
         223 +            for t in types
         224 +        ],
         225 +        "objects": [
         226 +            {
         227 +                "name": o.name,
         228 +                "type": o.type.name,
         229 +                "features": [float(v) for v in state.data[o]],
         230 +            }
         231 +            for o in sorted(state.data, key=lambda o: o.name)
         232 +        ],
         233 +    }
         234 +
         235 +
         236 +def _encode(obj: Any) -> Any:
         237 +    """Encode values as tagged JSON (mirrors robocode.utils.env_server)."""
         238 +    if isinstance(obj, _ObjectCentricState):
         239 +        return {_OCS_TAG: _ocs_to_payload(obj)}
         240 +    if isinstance(obj, np.generic):
         241 +        return obj.item()
         242 +    if isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
         243 +        return {_NDARRAY_TAG: obj.tolist(), "dtype": str(obj.dtype)}
         244 +    if isinstance(obj, dict):
         245 +        return {key: _encode(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
         246 +    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
         247 +        return [_encode(value) for value in obj]
         248 +    return obj
         249 +
         250 +
         251 +def _decode(obj: Any) -> Any:
         252 +    """Decode tagged JSON (mirrors robocode.utils.env_server)."""
         253 +    if isinstance(obj, dict):
         254 +        if _OCS_TAG in obj:
         255 +            return _ocs_from_payload(obj[_OCS_TAG])
         256 +        if _NDARRAY_TAG in obj:
         257 +            return np.array(obj[_NDARRAY_TAG], dtype=np.dtype(obj["dtype"]))
         258 +        return {key: _decode(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
         259 +    if isinstance(obj, list):
         260 +        return [_decode(value) for value in obj]
         261 +    return obj
         262 +
         263 +
         264 +def _encode_ref(obj: Any) -> Any:
         265 +    """Encode args/targets for the remote-object proxy commands.
         266 +
         267 +    Same as ``_encode`` but ``_RemoteHandle`` objects serialize to their
         268 +    ``{"__handle__": id}`` token so the host resolves them from its registry.
         269 +    Used only by devectorize/vectorize/getattr/call requests.
         270 +    """
         271 +    if isinstance(obj, _RemoteHandle):
         272 +        return {_HANDLE_TAG: obj._handle_id}  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         273 +    if isinstance(obj, _ObjectCentricState):
         274 +        return {_OCS_TAG: _ocs_to_payload(obj)}
         275 +    if isinstance(obj, np.generic):
         276 +        return obj.item()
         277 +    if isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
         278 +        return {_NDARRAY_TAG: obj.tolist(), "dtype": str(obj.dtype)}
         279 +    if isinstance(obj, dict):
         280 +        return {key: _encode_ref(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
         281 +    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
         282 +        return [_encode_ref(value) for value in obj]
         283 +    if isinstance(obj, (set, frozenset)):
         284 +        return {_SET_TAG: [_encode_ref(value) for value in obj]}
         285 +    return obj
         286 +
         287 +
         288 +class SpaceInfo:
         289 +    """Metadata for a Box space: shape, low, high, dtype, and sample()."""
         290 +
         291 +    def __init__(self, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
         292 +        if spec["type"] != "Box":
         293 +            raise TypeError(
         294 +                f"Unsupported space type {spec['type']!r}; extend SpaceInfo "
         295 +                "alongside the server's serialize_space"
         296 +            )
         297 +        self.shape: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(spec["shape"])
         298 +        self.dtype: np.dtype[Any] = np.dtype(spec["dtype"])
         299 +        self.low: np.ndarray = np.array(spec["low"], dtype=self.dtype)
         300 +        self.high: np.ndarray = np.array(spec["high"], dtype=self.dtype)
         301 +
         302 +    def sample(self, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
         303 +        """Sample uniformly between low and high."""
         304 +        if rng is None:
         305 +            rng = np.random.default_rng()
         306 +        return rng.uniform(self.low, self.high).astype(self.dtype)
         307 +
         308 +
         309 +class _RemoteHandle:
         310 +    """A reference to a host-side object, used over the env server.
         311 +
         312 +    Attribute access and calls are proxied to the host: ``handle.method(...)``
         313 +    issues a ``getattr`` (returning another handle for the bound method) then a
         314 +    ``call``. Returned values are decoded the same way as any response, so a
         315 +    scalar/ndarray comes back inline and another object comes back as a nested
         316 +    ``_RemoteHandle``. Private/dunder attributes are refused client-side, both
         317 +    to avoid surprise round-trips and to mirror the host security guard.
         318 +    """
         319 +
         320 +    def __init__(self, client: "BlackboxEnv", handle_id: str) -> None:
         321 +        # Use object.__setattr__-free plain assignment; __getattr__ only fires
         322 +        # for names not found normally, and these two are set here.
         323 +        self._client = client
         324 +        self._handle_id = handle_id
         325 +
         326 +    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
         327 +        if name.startswith("_"):
         328 +            raise AttributeError(
         329 +                f"refusing private/dunder attribute access on remote handle: "
         330 +                f"{name!r}"
         331 +            )
         332 +        response = self._client._request(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         333 +            {
         334 +                "cmd": "getattr",
         335 +                "target": {_HANDLE_TAG: self._handle_id},
         336 +                "name": name,
         337 +            }
         338 +        )
         339 +        return self._client._decode_ref(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         340 +            response["result"]
         341 +        )
         342 +
         343 +    def __call__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
         344 +        response = self._client._request(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         345 +            {
         346 +                "cmd": "call",
         347 +                "target": {_HANDLE_TAG: self._handle_id},
         348 +                "args": _encode_ref(list(args)),
         349 +                "kwargs": _encode_ref(kwargs),
         350 +            }
         351 +        )
         352 +        return self._client._decode_ref(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         353 +            response["result"]
         354 +        )

         357 +class _RemoteModule:
         358 +    """A reference to a whitelisted host module (e.g. crv_motion_planning).
         359 +
         360 +    Attribute access proxies a ``getattr`` against the ``{"__module__": name}``
         361 +    target, so ``module.plan_crv_actions`` returns a callable handle the agent
         362 +    can invoke. Mirrors how a remote-module primitive is used at eval time,
         363 +    where ``primitives['crv_motion_planning']`` is the real module.
         364 +    """
         365 +
         366 +    def __init__(self, client: "BlackboxEnv", short_name: str) -> None:
         367 +        self._client = client
         368 +        self._short_name = short_name
         369 +
         370 +    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
         371 +        if name.startswith("_"):
         372 +            raise AttributeError(
         373 +                f"refusing private/dunder attribute access on remote module: "
         374 +                f"{name!r}"
         375 +            )
         376 +        response = self._client._request(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         377 +            {
         378 +                "cmd": "getattr",
         379 +                "target": {_MODULE_TAG: self._short_name},
         380 +                "name": name,
         381 +            }
         382 +        )
         383 +        return self._client._decode_ref(  # pylint: disable=protected-access
         384 +            response["result"]
         385 +        )
         386 +
         387 +
         388 +class _BlackboxObservationSpace(SpaceInfo):
         389 +    """Box-space metadata plus client-backed devectorize/vectorize.
         390 +
         391 +    Stands in for the eval-time ``ObjectCentricBoxSpace``: it keeps the
         392 +    shape/low/high/dtype/sample() of a plain ``SpaceInfo`` and adds
         393 +    ``devectorize(obs)`` / ``vectorize(ocs)`` that proxy to the host. The agent
         394 +    writes ``observation_space.devectorize(obs)`` exactly as it would at eval.
         395 +    """
         396 +
         397 +    def __init__(self, spec: dict[str, Any], client: "BlackboxEnv") -> None:
         398 +        super().__init__(spec)
         399 +        self._client = client
         400 +
         401 +    def devectorize(self, obs: Any) -> Any:
         402 +        """Return an object-centric view of *obs* as a remote handle."""
         403 +        return self._client.devectorize(obs)
         404 +
         405 +    def vectorize(self, state: Any) -> np.ndarray:
         406 +        """Return the flat observation vector for an object-centric state."""
         407 +        return self._client.vectorize(state)
         408 +
         409 +
         410 +class _ObjectCentricObservationSpace:
         411 +    """Client-side view of a variable-count env's ObjectCentricStateSpace.
         412 +
         413 +    The observation is already an object-centric state (reconstructed locally from the
         414 +    wire), so this space has no fixed shape/vector: it exposes the domain ``types`` and
         415 +    ``type_features`` the program needs to enumerate objects, matching the eval-time
         416 +    ``observation_space.types``. There is no ``devectorize`` -- the state is not a
         417 +    vector.
         418 +    """
         419 +
         420 +    def __init__(self, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
         421 +        self._type_by_name, self._type_features = _build_local_types(spec["types"])
         422 +
         423 +    @property
         424 +    def types(self) -> set[_Type]:
         425 +        """The domain object types (matches the eval-time observation_space.types)."""
         426 +        return set(self._type_features)
         427 +
         428 +    @property
         429 +    def type_features(self) -> dict[_Type, list[str]]:
         430 +        """Feature names for each type."""
         431 +        return {t: list(f) for t, f in self._type_features.items()}
         432 +
         433 +    def get_type(self, name: str) -> _Type:
         434 +        """The domain type with the given name (e.g. ``"rectangle"``)."""
         435 +        return self._type_by_name[name]
         436 +
         437 +
         438 +class BlackboxEnv:
         439 +    """A live environment instance, accessed over the wire."""
         440 +
         441 +    def __init__(self, meta: dict[str, Any], sandbox_root: Any = None) -> None:
         442 +        obs_spec = meta["observation_space"]
         443 +        self._strict = bool(meta.get("strict", False))
         444 +        # A variable-count env sends object-centric states, reconstructed locally; a
         445 +        # fixed-count env sends Box vectors as before.
         446 +        self._object_centric = obs_spec.get("type") == "ObjectCentric"
         447 +        if self._object_centric:
         448 +            self.observation_space: Any = _ObjectCentricObservationSpace(obs_spec)
         449 +        elif self._strict:
         450 +            # Strict blackbox exposes only generic array metadata. In particular,
         451 +            # do not attach the host-backed devectorize/vectorize helpers that make
         452 +            # the legacy blackbox convenient but confound the isolation ablation.
         453 +            self.observation_space = SpaceInfo(obs_spec)
         454 +        else:
         455 +            self.observation_space = _BlackboxObservationSpace(obs_spec, self)
         456 +        self.action_space = SpaceInfo(meta["action_space"])
         457 +        self.max_steps: int | None = meta["max_steps"]
         458 +        # How make_primitives rebuilds the eval-time primitives dict (see
         459 +        # robocode.primitives.blackbox_primitive_manifest). Empty when the
         460 +        # run configures no primitives.
         461 +        self._primitive_manifest: list[dict[str, Any]] = meta.get("primitives", [])
         462 +        # Where render_policy looks for approach.py and make_primitives imports
         463 +        # generic primitive sources; the sandbox dir in real runs (set by
         464 +        # make_env), the current dir for ad-hoc construction.
         465 +        self._sandbox_root = (
         466 +            Path(sandbox_root) if sandbox_root is not None else Path.cwd()
         467 +        )
         468 +        self._token: str = meta["token"]
         469 +        self._sock = socket.create_connection((meta["host"], meta["port"]))
         470 +        self._file = self._sock.makefile("rwb")
         471 +
         472 +    def _request(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
         473 +        payload["token"] = self._token
         474 +        self._file.write(json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
         475 +        self._file.flush()
         476 +        line = self._file.readline()
         477 +        if not line:
         478 +            raise RuntimeError("Connection to the environment server was closed")
         479 +        response = json.loads(line)
         480 +        if "error" in response:
         481 +            raise RuntimeError(f"Environment server error: {response['error']}")
         482 +        return _decode(response)
         483 +
         484 +    def _decode_ref(self, obj: Any) -> Any:
         485 +        """Decode a remote-command result, mapping handles to _RemoteHandle.
         486 +
         487 +        ``_request`` already ran ``_decode`` over the response (so ndarrays are
         488 +        arrays), but it leaves ``{"__handle__": id}`` dicts intact since it does
         489 +        not know the handle tag. Here we turn those into ``_RemoteHandle``
         490 +        objects and recurse through the remaining containers.
         491 +        """
         492 +        if isinstance(obj, dict):
         493 +            if _HANDLE_TAG in obj:
         494 +                return _RemoteHandle(self, obj[_HANDLE_TAG])
         495 +            if _SET_TAG in obj:
         496 +                return {self._decode_ref(value) for value in obj[_SET_TAG]}
         497 +            return {key: self._decode_ref(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
         498 +        if isinstance(obj, list):
         499 +            return [self._decode_ref(value) for value in obj]
         500 +        return obj
         501 +
         502 +    def devectorize(self, obs: Any) -> _RemoteHandle:
         503 +        """Return an object-centric view of *obs* (a remote ObjectCentricState).
         504 +
         505 +        Proxies ``observation_space.devectorize`` to the host. The returned
         506 +        handle exposes the public ObjectCentricState API (``get_object_names``,
         507 +        ``get_object_from_name``, ``get_objects``, ``get``, ``set``, ``copy``,
         508 +        ...) over the wire. Pass it straight to the CRV planners from
         509 +        ``make_primitives``.
         510 +        """
         511 +        response = self._request(
         512 +            {"cmd": "devectorize", "obs": _encode(np.asarray(obs))}
         513 +        )
         514 +        return self._decode_ref(response["result"])
         515 +
         516 +    def vectorize(self, state: Any) -> np.ndarray:
         517 +        """Return the flat observation vector for an object-centric state handle."""
         518 +        response = self._request({"cmd": "vectorize", "state": _encode_ref(state)})
         519 +        return self._decode_ref(response["result"])
         520 +
         521 +    def reset(
         522 +        self, seed: int | None = None, options: dict[str, Any] | None = None
         523 +    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]:
         524 +        """Reset the environment; returns (obs, info)."""
         525 +        response = self._request({"cmd": "reset", "seed": seed, "options": options})
         526 +        return response["obs"], response["info"]
         527 +
         528 +    def step(self, action: Any) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, dict[str, Any]]:
         529 +        """Step the environment; returns (obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info)."""
         530 +        action = np.asarray(action, dtype=self.action_space.dtype)
         531 +        response = self._request({"cmd": "step", "action": _encode(action)})
         532 +        return (
         533 +            response["obs"],
         534 +            response["reward"],
         535 +            response["terminated"],
         536 +            response["truncated"],
         537 +            response["info"],
         538 +        )
         539 +
         540 +    def get_state(self) -> Any:
         541 +        """Return a snapshot of the full environment state.
         542 +
         543 +        A Box vector for a fixed-count env; a local ObjectCentricState for a
         544 +        variable-count env (reconstructed by ``_decode``).
         545 +        """
         546 +        return self._request({"cmd": "get_state"})["state"]
         547 +
         548 +    def _encode_state(self, state: Any) -> Any:
         549 +        """Encode a state for the wire: an object-centric state or a Box vector."""
         550 +        if isinstance(state, _ObjectCentricState):
         551 +            return _encode(state)
         552 +        return _encode(np.asarray(state))
         553 +
         554 +    def render_state(
         555 +        self,
         556 +        seed: int = 42,
         557 +        state: Any = None,
         558 +        label: str = "",
         559 +        object_count: int | None = None,
         560 +    ) -> str:
         561 +        """Render a state on the host; returns a PNG path inside the sandbox.
         562 +
         563 +        Either pass ``seed`` to render the initial state after a reset (with
         564 +        ``object_count`` to pin a variable-count env's object count), or ``state`` (a
         565 +        flat list of floats, as from ``get_state().tolist()``) to render an arbitrary
         566 +        state. The path is relative to the sandbox dir.
         567 +        """
         568 +        if isinstance(state, _ObjectCentricState):
         569 +            state = _encode(state)  # tagged object-centric payload, decoded host-side
         570 +        elif isinstance(state, np.ndarray):
         571 +            state = state.tolist()
         572 +        return self._request(
         573 +            {
         574 +                "cmd": "render_state",
         575 +                "seed": seed,
         576 +                "state": state,
         577 +                "label": label,
         578 +                "object_count": object_count,
         579 +            }
         580 +        )["path"]
         581 +
         582 +    def render_policy(
         583 +        self,
         584 +        seed: int = 42,
         585 +        max_steps: int = 1000,
         586 +        max_frames: int = 100,
         587 +        approach_path: Any = None,
         588 +        object_count: int | None = None,
         589 +    ) -> list[str]:
         590 +        """Run an episode of approach.py here and render the visited states.
         591 +
         592 +        The policy runs in this process: only ``get_action`` (which needs the
         593 +        observation alone) executes locally, while each visited state is
         594 +        rendered on the host via ``render_state``. No approach code runs on the
         595 +        host, so a black-box agent cannot reach the env source through rendering.
         596 +        ``object_count`` pins a variable-count env's object count on the rollout reset.
         597 +        Returns the PNG paths (relative to the sandbox dir).
         598 +        """
         599 +        path = (
         600 +            Path(approach_path)
         601 +            if approach_path is not None
         602 +            else self._sandbox_root / "approach.py"
         603 +        )
         604 +        approach = _load_generated_approach(
         605 +            path, self.action_space, self.observation_space, self.make_primitives()
         606 +        )
         607 +        options = {"object_count": object_count} if object_count is not None else None
         608 +        obs, info = self.reset(seed=seed, options=options)
         609 +        approach.reset(obs, info)
         610 +        # Strict mode deliberately withholds raw state snapshots. Its observations
         611 +        # are nevertheless renderable, so use them to visualize a policy without
         612 +        # opening the get_state channel to agent scripts.
         613 +        states = [obs if self._strict else self.get_state()]
         614 +        for _ in range(max_steps):
         615 +            obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = self.step(
         616 +                approach.get_action(obs)
         617 +            )
         618 +            if hasattr(approach, "update"):
         619 +                approach.update(obs, reward, terminated or truncated, info)
         620 +            states.append(obs if self._strict else self.get_state())
         621 +            if terminated or truncated:
         622 +                break
         623 +        return [
         624 +            self.render_state(state=state, label=f"policy_seed{seed}_{i:04d}")
         625 +            for i, state in enumerate(states[:max_frames])
         626 +        ]
         627 +
         628 +    def set_state(self, state: Any) -> None:
         629 +        """Restore a state snapshot previously returned by get_state()."""
         630 +        self._request({"cmd": "set_state", "state": self._encode_state(state)})
         631 +
         632 +    def check_action_collision(self, state: Any, action: Any) -> bool:
         633 +        """Return True if taking *action* in *state* causes a collision.
         634 +
         635 +        Runs the env-dependent collision primitive on the host (the sandbox
         636 +        lacks the env source), against this connection's env. Mirrors the
         637 +        eval-time ``primitives['check_action_collision']`` callable, so test
         638 +        scripts that get it from ``make_primitives`` call it the same way.
         639 +        """
         640 +        response = self._request(
         641 +            {
         642 +                "cmd": "check_action_collision",
         643 +                "state": self._encode_state(state),
         644 +                "action": _encode(np.asarray(action, dtype=self.action_space.dtype)),
         645 +            }
         646 +        )
         647 +        return response["collision"]
         648 +
         649 +    def make_primitives(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
         650 +        """Build the eval-time primitives dict for this black-box env.
         651 +
         652 +        Black-box counterpart of ``robocode.primitives.build_primitives``:
         653 +        env-dependent primitives proxy to the host, while generic ones are
         654 +        imported from their copies under ``primitives/`` in the sandbox. Use
         655 +        it in test scripts so they exercise exactly the primitives the harness
         656 +        passes to ``GeneratedApproach`` at evaluation time::
         657 +
         658 +            from env_client import make_env
         659 +
         660 +            env = make_env()
         661 +            primitives = env.make_primitives()
         662 +        """
         663 +        sandbox_dir = str(self._sandbox_root.resolve())
         664 +        if sandbox_dir not in sys.path:
         665 +            sys.path.insert(0, sandbox_dir)
         666 +        primitives: dict[str, Any] = {}
         667 +        for spec in self._primitive_manifest:
         668 +            if spec["kind"] == "host_proxy":
         669 +                primitives[spec["name"]] = getattr(self, spec["name"])
         670 +            elif spec["kind"] == "remote_module":
         671 +                # The module source is withheld from the sandbox; reach it on
         672 +                # the host via a remote-module proxy (e.g. crv_motion_planning).
         673 +                primitives[spec["name"]] = _RemoteModule(self, spec["module"])
         674 +            else:
         675 +                module = importlib.import_module(f"primitives.{spec['module']}")
         676 +                primitives[spec["name"]] = (
         677 +                    module if spec["attr"] is None else getattr(module, spec["attr"])
         678 +                )
         679 +        return primitives
         680 +
         681 +    def close(self) -> None:
         682 +        """Close the connection (and the server-side environment)."""
         683 +        try:
         684 +            self._file.write(
         685 +                json.dumps({"cmd": "close", "token": self._token}).encode("utf-8")
         686 +                + b"\n"
         687 +            )

         690 +            # makefile() wraps a dup of the socket; close it too so the buffered
         691 +            # file object does not leak (ResourceWarning) when close() runs.
         692 +            self._file.close()
         693 +            self._sock.close()

         695 +    def __enter__(self) -> "BlackboxEnv":
         696 +        return self
         697 +
         698 +    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: Any) -> None:
         699 +        self.close()
         700 +
         701 +
         702 +def _load_generated_approach(
         703 +    path: Path, action_space: Any, observation_space: Any, primitives: dict[str, Any]
         704 +) -> Any:
         705 +    """Exec ``approach.py`` and instantiate its ``GeneratedApproach``.
         706 +
         707 +    Mirrors ``robocode.utils.episode.load_generated_approach``; duplicated here
         708 +    (like the codec above) because this module must stay importable with only
         709 +    the standard library and numpy, since it is copied standalone into the
         710 +    sandbox. Used only by ``render_policy`` for visual debugging.
         711 +    """
         712 +    sandbox_dir = str(path.resolve().parent)
         713 +    added = sandbox_dir not in sys.path
         714 +    if added:
         715 +        sys.path.insert(0, sandbox_dir)
         716 +    try:
         717 +        namespace: dict[str, Any] = {"__file__": str(path)}
         718 +        exec(  # pylint: disable=exec-used
         719 +            compile(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), str(path), "exec"), namespace
         720 +        )
         721 +    finally:
         722 +        if added:
         723 +            sys.path.remove(sandbox_dir)
         724 +    return namespace["GeneratedApproach"](
         725 +        action_space, observation_space, primitives=primitives
         726 +    )
         727 +
         728 +
         729 +def make_env(metadata_path: Any = None) -> BlackboxEnv:
         730 +    """Connect to the environment server; returns a fresh env instance.
         731 +
         732 +    *metadata_path* defaults to ``env_spaces.json`` next to this module
         733 +    (the agent's sandbox copy); the MCP server passes an explicit path.
         734 +    """
         735 +    path = Path(metadata_path) if metadata_path is not None else _METADATA_PATH
         736 +    meta = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
         737 +    return BlackboxEnv(meta, sandbox_root=path.parent)

          48 +            d["objective"].append((name, {f: _val(state, o, f) for f in
          49 +                                          ("x", "y", "z", "have_image_rover0", "have_image_rover1",
          50 +                                           "received_image")}))
          51 +        elif t == "sample":
          52 +            d["sample"].append((name, {f: _val(state, o, f) for f in
          53 +                                       ("x", "y", "z", "is_soil", "analyzed_rover0",
          54 +                                        "analyzed_rover1", "received_analysis")}))
          55 +        elif t == "obstacle":
          56 +            d["obstacle"].append((name, {f: _val(state, o, f) for f in
          57 +                                         ("x", "y", "z", "half_x", "half_y", "half_z")}))
          58 +    d["objective"].sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
          59 +    d["sample"].sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
          60 +    return d
          61 +
          62 +
          63 +def sense_offset(theta):
          64 +    # sensing point = base + R(theta) @ (-0.087, -0.012)
          65 +    c, s = math.cos(theta), math.sin(theta)
          66 +    return (-SENSE_BACK * c + SENSE_RIGHT * s, -SENSE_BACK * s - SENSE_RIGHT * c)
          67 +
          68 +
          69 +def seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, px, py):
          70 +    """Distance from point (px,py) to segments (ex,ey)->(tx,ty); ex,ey arrays."""
          71 +    dx = tx - ex
          72 +    dy = ty - ey
          73 +    L2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + 1e-12
          74 +    t = ((px - ex) * dx + (py - ey) * dy) / L2
          75 +    t = np.clip(t, 0.0, 1.0)
          76 +    qx = ex + t * dx - px
          77 +    qy = ey + t * dy - py
          78 +    return np.sqrt(qx * qx + qy * qy)
          79 +
          80 +
          81 +def bfs_field(free, init):
          82 +    """Min steps field: D(x) = min over y within Chebyshev-4 of D(y)+1, restricted to free."""
          83 +    D = np.where(free, init, INF)
          84 +    for _ in range(400):
          85 +        nb = minimum_filter(D, size=2 * STEP_CELLS + 1, mode="constant", cval=INF) + 1.0
          86 +        nb[~free] = INF
          87 +        D2 = np.minimum(D, nb)
          88 +        if np.array_equal(D2, D):
          89 +            break
          90 +        D = D2
          91 +    return D
          92 +
          93 +
          94 +def to_cell(x, y):
          95 +    i = int(round((x + LIM) / RES))
          96 +    j = int(round((y + LIM) / RES))
          97 +    return min(max(i, 0), N - 1), min(max(j, 0), N - 1)

          99 +
         100 +class GeneratedApproach:
         101 +    def __init__(self, action_space, observation_space, primitives):
         102 +        self.action_space = action_space
         103 +        self.observation_space = observation_space
         104 +
         105 +    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ setup
         106 +    def reset(self, state, info):
         107 +        d = parse(state)
         108 +        self.d0 = d
         109 +        self.rovers = ["rover0", "rover1"]
         110 +        self.home = {r: (d["rover"][r]["x"], d["rover"][r]["y"], d["rover"][r]["theta"])
         111 +                     for r in self.rovers}
         112 +        self.lander = d["lander"]
         113 +        self.mounds = []
         114 +        self.pillars = []
         115 +        for _, ob in d["obstacle"]:
         116 +            if ob["half_x"] > 0.1:
         117 +                self.mounds.append(ob)
         118 +            else:
         119 +                self.pillars.append(ob)
         120 +        self.objs = [n for n, _ in d["objective"]]
         121 +        self.obj_pos = {n: (o["x"], o["y"]) for n, o in d["objective"]}
         122 +        self.samples = {n: (o["x"], o["y"], o["is_soil"] > 0.5) for n, o in d["sample"]}
         123 +        self._build_free()
         124 +        self.sense = {r: sense_offset(self.home[r][2]) for r in self.rovers}
         125 +        self.side = {r: (1 if self.home[r][0] > 0 else -1) for r in self.rovers}
         126 +        self.free_r = {r: self.free & ((GX * self.side[r]) > 0) for r in self.rovers}
         127 +        self._build_regions()
         128 +        self._plan()
         129 +        self.stage_fields = {}
         130 +        self.t = 0
         131 +
         132 +    def _build_free(self):
         133 +        free = np.ones((N, N), dtype=bool)
         134 +        free &= np.abs(GX) >= WALL_X
         135 +        for m in self.mounds:
         136 +            dx = np.maximum(np.abs(GX - m["x"]) - m["half_x"], 0)
         137 +            dy = np.maximum(np.abs(GY - m["y"]) - m["half_y"], 0)
         138 +            free &= np.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) >= MOUND_CLEAR
         139 +        for p in self.pillars:
         140 +            free &= np.hypot(GX - p["x"], GY - p["y"]) >= PILLAR_CLEAR
         141 +        lx, ly = self.lander
         142 +        free &= np.hypot(GX - lx, GY - ly) >= LANDER_CLEAR
         143 +        self.free = free
         144 +
         145 +    def _vis_mask(self, r, tx, ty, rng, other_rover=None):
         146 +        ox, oy = self.sense[r]
         147 +        ex = GX + ox
         148 +        ey = GY + oy
         149 +        m = np.hypot(ex - tx, ey - ty) <= rng
         150 +        for p in self.pillars:
         151 +            m &= seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, p["x"], p["y"]) > LOS_PILLAR
         152 +        if other_rover is not None:
         153 +            m &= seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, other_rover[0], other_rover[1]) > LOS_ROVER
         154 +        return m
         155 +
         156 +    def _build_regions(self):
         157 +        self.obj_vis = {}
         158 +        self.send_reg = {}
         159 +        for r in self.rovers:
         160 +            fr = self.free_r[r]
         161 +            for o in self.objs:
         162 +                tx, ty = self.obj_pos[o]
         163 +                self.obj_vis[(r, o)] = self._vis_mask(r, tx, ty, OBJ_RANGE) & fr
         164 +            other = [q for q in self.rovers if q != r][0]
         165 +            oh = self.home[other]
         166 +            self.send_reg[r] = self._vis_mask(r, self.lander[0], self.lander[1], LANDER_RANGE,
         167 +                                              other_rover=(oh[0], oh[1])) & fr
         168 +        self.samp_reg = {}
         169 +        for s, (sx, sy, _) in self.samples.items():
         170 +            self.samp_reg[s] = (np.hypot(GX - sx, GY - sy) <= SAMPLE_RANGE) & self.free
         171 +        # home & send-then-home fields
         172 +        self.V_home = {}
         173 +        self.V_send = {}
         174 +        for r in self.rovers:
         175 +            hx, hy, _ = self.home[r]
         176 +            init = np.full((N, N), INF)
         177 +            hm = (np.hypot(GX - hx, GY - hy) <= 0.2) & self.free_r[r]
         178 +            hi, hj = to_cell(hx, hy)
         179 +            hm[hi, hj] = True
         180 +            init[hm] = 0.0
         181 +            Vh = bfs_field(self.free_r[r], init)
         182 +            self.V_home[r] = Vh
         183 +            init2 = np.where(self.send_reg[r], Vh, INF)
         184 +            self.V_send[r] = bfs_field(self.free_r[r], init2)
         185 +
         186 +    # -------------------------------------------------------------- planning
         187 +    def _task_region(self, r, task, held=()):
         188 +        kind, name = task
         189 +        if kind == "obj":
         190 +            reg = self.obj_vis[(r, name)].copy()
         191 +            # prefer cells where this objective is the nearest visible non-held one
         192 +            ox, oy = self.sense[r]
         193 +            tx, ty = self.obj_pos[name]
         194 +            dme = np.hypot(GX + ox - tx, GY + oy - ty)
         195 +            for o2 in self.objs:
         196 +                if o2 == name or o2 in held:
         197 +                    continue
         198 +                t2x, t2y = self.obj_pos[o2]
         199 +                d2 = np.hypot(GX + ox - t2x, GY + oy - t2y)
         200 +                reg &= ~(self.obj_vis[(r, o2)] & (d2 < dme))
         201 +            return reg
         202 +        return self.samp_reg[name] & self.free_r[self.rovers[0] if False else r]
         203 +
         204 +    def _candidates(self, reg, k=8):
         205 +        idx = np.argwhere(reg)
         206 +        if len(idx) == 0:
         207 +            return []
         208 +        if len(idx) <= k:
         209 +            return [tuple(x) for x in idx]
         210 +        pts = idx.astype(float)
         211 +        chosen = [len(idx) // 2]
         212 +        dmin = np.linalg.norm(pts - pts[chosen[0]], axis=1)
         213 +        while len(chosen) < k:
         214 +            nxt = int(np.argmax(dmin))
         215 +            chosen.append(nxt)
         216 +            dmin = np.minimum(dmin, np.linalg.norm(pts - pts[nxt], axis=1))
         217 +        return [tuple(idx[c]) for c in chosen]
         218 +
         219 +    def _point_field(self, r, cell):
         220 +        init = np.full((N, N), INF)
         221 +        init[cell] = 0.0
         222 +        return bfs_field(self.free_r[r], init)
         223 +
         224 +    def _rover_tasks(self, r):
         225 +        tasks = []
         226 +        for o in self.objs:
         227 +            if self.obj_vis[(r, o)].any():
         228 +                tasks.append(("obj", o))
         229 +        for s, (sx, sy, soil) in self.samples.items():
         230 +            if sx * self.side[r] > 0 and (self.samp_reg[s] & self.free_r[r]).any():
         231 +                tasks.append(("stone" if not soil else "soil", s))
         232 +        return tasks
         233 +
         234 +    def _held_karp(self, r, tasks):
         235 +        """Return dict: frozenset(task idx) -> (cost, order list)."""
         236 +        hx, hy, _ = self.home[r]
         237 +        start = to_cell(hx, hy)
         238 +        nodes = []  # (task_idx, cell)
         239 +        for ti, t in enumerate(tasks):
         240 +            reg = self._task_region(r, (t[0] if t[0] == "obj" else "samp", t[1]))
         241 +            if not reg.any():
         242 +                reg = self.obj_vis[(r, t[1])] if t[0] == "obj" else self.samp_reg[t[1]] & self.free_r[r]
         243 +            cands = self._candidates(reg, 8)
         244 +            # add cells closest to start
         245 +            Fstart = None
         246 +            for c in cands:
         247 +                nodes.append((ti, c))
         248 +        fields = [self._point_field(r, c) for _, c in nodes]
         249 +        nn = len(nodes)
         250 +        dist = np.full((nn, nn), INF)
         251 +        for a in range(nn):
         252 +            for b in range(nn):
         253 +                dist[a, b] = fields[b][nodes[a][1]]
         254 +        dstart = np.array([fields[b][start] for b in range(nn)])
         255 +        dend = np.array([self.V_send[r][nodes[a][1]] for a in range(nn)])
         256 +        T = len(tasks)
         257 +        kinds = [t[0] for t in tasks]
         258 +        # DP over masks
         259 +        best = {}
         260 +        for a in range(nn):
         261 +            m = 1 << nodes[a][0]
         262 +            v = dstart[a]
         263 +            key = (m, a)
         264 +            if v < best.get(key, (INF,))[0]:
         265 +                best[key] = (v, None)
         266 +        masks = sorted(set(k[0] for k in best))
         267 +        by_mask = {}
         268 +        for (m, a), v in best.items():
         269 +            by_mask.setdefault(m, {})[a] = v
         270 +        results = {0: (self.V_send[r][start], [])}
         271 +        order_masks = sorted(range(1 << T), key=lambda m: bin(m).count("1"))
         272 +        valid = {}
         273 +        for m in order_masks:
         274 +            ns = sum(1 for i in range(T) if m >> i & 1 and kinds[i] == "stone")
         275 +            nl = sum(1 for i in range(T) if m >> i & 1 and kinds[i] == "soil")
         276 +            valid[m] = ns <= 1 and nl <= 1
         277 +        for m in order_masks:
         278 +            if m == 0 or not valid[m] or m not in by_mask:
         279 +                continue
         280 +            ent = by_mask[m]
         281 +            # finalize
         282 +            bestfin = INF
         283 +            bestA = None
         284 +            for a, (v, _) in ent.items():
         285 +                f = v + dend[a]
         286 +                if f < bestfin:
         287 +                    bestfin, bestA = f, a
         288 +            if bestA is not None and bestfin < INF:
         289 +                # reconstruct order
         290 +                order = []
         291 +                mm, aa = m, bestA
         292 +                while aa is not None:
         293 +                    order.append(nodes[aa])
         294 +                    prev = by_mask[mm][aa][1]
         295 +                    mm = mm & ~(1 << nodes[aa][0])
         296 +                    aa = prev
         297 +                results[m] = (bestfin, [tasks[ti] for ti, _ in reversed(order)])
         298 +            for a, (v, _) in ent.items():
         299 +                for b in range(nn):
         300 +                    tb = nodes[b][0]
         301 +                    if m >> tb & 1:
         302 +                        continue
         303 +                    m2 = m | (1 << tb)
         304 +                    if not valid[m2]:
         305 +                        continue
         306 +                    nv = v + dist[a, b]
         307 +                    cur = by_mask.setdefault(m2, {})
         308 +                    if b not in cur or nv < cur[b][0]:
         309 +                        cur[b] = (nv, a)
         310 +        return results
         311 +
         312 +    def _plan(self):
         313 +        tasks = {r: self._rover_tasks(r) for r in self.rovers}
         314 +        hk = {r: self._held_karp(r, tasks[r]) for r in self.rovers}
         315 +        best = (INF, None)
         316 +        objs = self.objs
         317 +        r0, r1 = self.rovers
         318 +        for m0, (c0, ord0) in hk[r0].items():
         319 +            s0 = set(t for t in ord0)
         320 +            for m1, (c1, ord1) in hk[r1].items():
         321 +                s1 = set(t for t in ord1)
         322 +                allt = s0 | s1
         323 +                ok = all(("obj", o) in allt for o in objs)
         324 +                ok = ok and any(t[0] == "stone" for t in allt) and any(t[0] == "soil" for t in allt)
         325 +                if not ok:
         326 +                    continue
         327 +                # penalize duplicates slightly
         328 +                cost = max(c0, c1) + 0.01 * (c0 + c1) + 0.001 * len(s0 & s1)
         329 +                if cost < best[0]:
         330 +                    best = (cost, (ord0, ord1))
         331 +        if best[1] is None:
         332 +            self.orders = {r: [] for r in self.rovers}
         333 +        else:
         334 +            self.orders = {r0: list(best[1][0]), r1: list(best[1][1])}
         335 +        self.plan_cost = best[0]
         336 +        # exact stage fields per rover (backward DP)
         337 +        self.fields = {}
         338 +        for r in self.rovers:
         339 +            self.fields[r] = self._stage_fields(r, self.orders[r])
         340 +
         341 +    def _stage_fields(self, r, order):
         342 +        """fields[i] = cost-to-go when tasks order[i:] remain (then send+home)."""
         343 +        k = len(order)
         344 +        fields = [None] * (k + 1)
         345 +        regs = [None] * k
         346 +        fields[k] = self.V_send[r]
         347 +        for i in range(k - 1, -1, -1):
         348 +            t = order[i]
         349 +            held = tuple(o for kk, o in order[:i] if kk == "obj")
         350 +            if t[0] == "obj":
         351 +                reg = self._task_region(r, ("obj", t[1]), held)
         352 +                if not reg.any():
         353 +                    reg = self.obj_vis[(r, t[1])]
         354 +            else:
         355 +                reg = self.samp_reg[t[1]] & self.free_r[r]
         356 +            regs[i] = reg
         357 +            init = np.where(reg, fields[i + 1], INF)
         358 +            fields[i] = bfs_field(self.free_r[r], init)
         359 +        return {"fields": fields, "regs": regs, "order": order}
         360 +
         361 +    # -------------------------------------------------------------- execution
         362 +    def _visible_objs(self, r, x, y, theta):
         363 +        ox, oy = sense_offset(theta)
         364 +        ex, ey = x + ox, y + oy
         365 +        res = []
         366 +        for o in self.objs:
         367 +            tx, ty = self.obj_pos[o]
         368 +            dd = math.hypot(ex - tx, ey - ty)
         369 +            if dd > OBJ_RANGE + 0.03:
         370 +                continue
         371 +            ok = True
         372 +            for p in self.pillars:
         373 +                if float(seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, p["x"], p["y"])) <= LOS_PILLAR - 0.01:
         374 +                    ok = False
         375 +                    break
         376 +            if ok:
         377 +                res.append((dd, o))
         378 +        res.sort()
         379 +        return res
         380 +
         381 +    def _lander_visible(self, r, x, y, theta, other):
         382 +        ox, oy = sense_offset(theta)
         383 +        ex, ey = x + ox, y + oy
         384 +        tx, ty = self.lander
         385 +        if math.hypot(ex - tx, ey - ty) > LANDER_RANGE + 0.03:
         386 +            return False
         387 +        for p in self.pillars:
         388 +            if float(seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, p["x"], p["y"])) <= LOS_PILLAR - 0.01:
         389 +                return False
         390 +        if float(seg_dist_grid(ex, ey, tx, ty, other[0], other[1])) <= LOS_ROVER - 0.03:
         391 +            return False
         392 +        return True
         393 +
         394 +    def _task_done(self, d, r, t):
         395 +        if t[0] == "obj":
         396 +            for n, o in d["objective"]:
         397 +                if n == t[1]:
         398 +                    return o["have_image_" + r] > 0.5 or o["received_image"] > 0.5
         399 +            return True
         400 +        for n, s in d["sample"]:
         401 +            if n == t[1]:
         402 +                if s["analyzed_" + r] > 0.5:
         403 +                    return True
         404 +        # any analysis of the same kind already done by anyone counts
         405 +        soil = t[0] == "soil"
         406 +        for n, s in d["sample"]:
         407 +            if (s["is_soil"] > 0.5) == soil and (s["analyzed_rover0"] > 0.5 or s["analyzed_rover1"] > 0.5):
         408 +                return True
         409 +        return False
         410 +
         411 +    def get_action(self, state):
         412 +        d = parse(state)
         413 +        act = np.zeros(8, dtype=np.float32)
         414 +        for k, r in enumerate(self.rovers):
         415 +            other = [q for q in self.rovers if q != r][0]
         416 +            ro = d["rover"][r]
         417 +            orv = d["rover"][other]
         418 +            dx, dy, op = self._rover_action(d, r, ro, (orv["x"], orv["y"]))
         419 +            act[4 * k + 0] = dx
         420 +            act[4 * k + 1] = dy
         421 +            act[4 * k + 2] = 0.0
         422 +            act[4 * k + 3] = SEL[op]
         423 +        self.t += 1
         424 +        return act
         425 +
         426 +    def _rover_action(self, d, r, ro, other_xy):
         427 +        plan = self.fields[r]
         428 +        order = plan["order"]
         429 +        stage = 0
         430 +        while stage < len(order) and self._task_done(d, r, order[stage]):
         431 +            stage += 1
         432 +        x, y, th = ro["x"], ro["y"], ro["theta"]
         433 +        i, j = to_cell(x, y)
         434 +        # pending results to send?
         435 +        pending = False
         436 +        for n, o in d["objective"]:
         437 +            if o["have_image_" + r] > 0.5 and o["received_image"] < 0.5:
         438 +                pending = True
         439 +        for n, s in d["sample"]:
         440 +            if s["analyzed_" + r] > 0.5 and s["received_analysis"] < 0.5:
         441 +                pending = True
         442 +        if stage < len(order):
         443 +            F = plan["fields"][stage]
         444 +            reg = plan["regs"][stage]
         445 +        else:
         446 +            if pending:
         447 +                F = self.V_send[r]
         448 +                reg = None
         449 +            else:
         450 +                F = self.V_home[r]
         451 +                reg = None
         452 +        # choose next cell
         453 +        best = None
         454 +        i0, i1 = max(i - STEP_CELLS, 0), min(i + STEP_CELLS, N - 1)
         455 +        j0, j1 = max(j - STEP_CELLS, 0), min(j + STEP_CELLS, N - 1)
         456 +        sub = F[i0:i1 + 1, j0:j1 + 1]
         457 +        cur = F[i, j]
         458 +        # stay if current cell is a goal (in region) for this stage
         459 +        ready = True
         460 +        if stage < len(order):
         461 +            t0 = order[stage]
         462 +            if t0[0] == "obj":
         463 +                ready = ro["calibrated"] > 0.5
         464 +            else:
         465 +                ready = ro["store_full"] < 0.5
         466 +        if (not ready) and reg is not None and reg[i, j]:
         467 +            rsub = reg[i0:i1 + 1, j0:j1 + 1]
         468 +            sub = np.where(rsub, sub, INF)
         469 +        mn = sub.min()
         470 +        cands = np.argwhere(sub <= mn + 1e-9)
         471 +        # tie-break: prefer staying close (smaller move) -- then toward straight
         472 +        bestc = None
         473 +        bestscore = None
         474 +        for ci, cj in cands:
         475 +            ii, jj = i0 + ci, j0 + cj
         476 +            score = max(abs(ii - i), abs(jj - j)) * 0.01 + math.hypot(ii - i, jj - j) * 0.001
         477 +            if bestscore is None or score < bestscore:
         478 +                bestscore, bestc = score, (ii, jj)
         479 +        ti, tj = bestc
         480 +        if cur <= mn + 1e-9 and reg is not None and reg[i, j]:
         481 +            ti, tj = i, j
         482 +        nx, ny = COORDS[ti], COORDS[tj]
         483 +        mdx = float(np.clip(nx - x, -0.2, 0.2))
         484 +        mdy = float(np.clip(ny - y, -0.2, 0.2))
         485 +        px, py = x + mdx, y + mdy
         486 +        # ---- operator selection (evaluated at post-move position)
         487 +        op = "noop"
         488 +        vis = self._visible_objs(r, px, py, th)
         489 +        held = set(n for n, o in d["objective"] if o["have_image_" + r] > 0.5)
         490 +        notheld = [o for dd, o in vis if o not in held]
         491 +        need_imgs = [t[1] for t in order[stage:] if t[0] == "obj"]
         492 +        cal = ro["calibrated"] > 0.5
         493 +        store_full = ro["store_full"] > 0.5
         494 +        if stage < len(order):
         495 +            t = order[stage]
         496 +            if t[0] in ("stone", "soil"):
         497 +                sx, sy, _ = self.samples[t[1]]
         498 +                if not store_full and math.hypot(px - sx, py - sy) <= 0.24:
         499 +                    return mdx, mdy, "sample"
         500 +        if cal and notheld and notheld[0] in need_imgs:
         501 +            return mdx, mdy, "image"
         502 +        if store_full:
         503 +            return mdx, mdy, "drop"
         504 +        if not cal and need_imgs and vis:
         505 +            return mdx, mdy, "calibrate"
         506 +        if pending and self._lander_visible(r, px, py, th, other_xy):
         507 +            return mdx, mdy, "send"
         508 +        return mdx, mdy, op

diff --git a/pA_lib.py b/pA_lib.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..76ba042
--- /dev/null
+++ b/pA_lib.py
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
           1 +from env_client import make_env
           2 +import numpy as np
           3 +class P:
           4 +    def __init__(self,seed=0):
           5 +        self.env=make_env(); self.reset(seed)
           6 +    def reset(self,seed=0):
           7 +        self.obs,_=self.env.reset(seed=seed); return self
           8 +    def st(self,name):
           9 +        o=self.obs.get_object_from_name(name)
          10 +        out={}
          11 +        for f in ['x','y','theta','store_full','calibrated','at_home','z','half_x','half_y','half_z']:
          12 +            try: out[f]=float(self.obs.get(o,f))
          13 +            except Exception: pass
          14 +        return out
          15 +    def pos(self,i):
          16 +        s=self.st('rover%d'%i); return np.array([s['x'],s['y'],s['theta']])
          17 +    def step(self,a0=(0,0,0,0),a1=(0,0,0,0)):
          18 +        a=np.array(list(a0)+list(a1),dtype=np.float32)
          19 +        self.obs,r,te,tr,info=self.env.step(a); return r,te,tr
          20 +    def mv(self,i,dx,dy,dth=0,sel=0):
          21 +        a=[dx,dy,dth,sel]; z=[0,0,0,0]
          22 +        before=self.pos(i)
          23 +        self.step(a,z) if i==0 else self.step(z,a)
          24 +        after=self.pos(i)
          25 +        return after, not np.allclose(before,after,atol=1e-6)
          26 +    def goto(self,i,x,y,th=None,maxit=200):
          27 +        """greedy; returns final pos; tries axis-sliding if blocked"""
          28 +        for _ in range(maxit):
          29 +            p=self.pos(i); d=np.array([x,y])-p[:2]
          30 +            dth=0 if th is None else ((th-p[2]+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi)
          31 +            if np.linalg.norm(d)<1e-4 and abs(dth)<1e-4: break
          32 +            dd=np.clip(d,-0.2,0.2); dt=np.clip(dth,-0.4,0.4)
          33 +            _,ok=self.mv(i,dd[0],dd[1],dt)
          34 +            if not ok:
          35 +                _,ok=self.mv(i,dd[0],0,0)
          36 +                if not ok: _,ok=self.mv(i,0,dd[1],0)
          37 +                if not ok: _,ok=self.mv(i,0,0,dt)
          38 +                if not ok: break
          39 +        return self.pos(i)
          40 +    def probe(self,i,dx,dy,dth=0,n=500):
          41 +        """step repeatedly until blocked"""
          42 +        for k in range(n):
          43 +            p,ok=self.mv(i,dx,dy,dth)
          44 +            if not ok: return p,k
          45 +        return p,n
          46 +    def bisect(self,i,ux,uy,lo=0.2):
          47 +        """from current pos, coarse probe in unit dir then refine to 1e-4"""
          48 +        s=0.2
          49 +        while s>1e-4:
          50 +            p,k=self.probe(i,ux*s,uy*s)
          51 +            s/=2
          52 +        return self.pos(i)

          16 +    _,ok=p.mv(1,0.2,0)

           1 +import numpy as np
           2 +L=np.array([-1.9,-2.0]); P=np.array([-0.135,-0.64]); d=(P-L)/np.linalg.norm(P-L); perp=np.array([-d[1],d[0]])
           3 +def segd(a,b,p):
           4 +    ab=b-a; t=np.clip(np.dot(p-a,ab)/np.dot(ab,ab),0,1); return np.linalg.norm(a+t*ab-p)
           5 +pil={'p6':np.array([-0.135,-0.64]),'p9':np.array([0.654,-0.199])}
           6 +for sv in np.arange(-0.2,0.2,0.02):
           7 +    q=L+3.5*d+sv*perp; e=q+np.array([0.087,0.012])  # theta=pi offset
           8 +    print(round(sv,2), {k:(round(segd(q,L,v),3),round(segd(e,L,v),3)) for k,v in pil.items()})
diff --git a/pB_lib.py b/pB_lib.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..00c0b1e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/pB_lib.py
@@ -0,0 +1,38 @@
           1 +import numpy as np
           2 +from env_client import make_env
           3 +SEL=dict(sample=-0.8333,cal=-0.5,img=-0.1667,noop=0,send=0.5,drop=0.8333)
           4 +def R(s,n):
           5 +    o=s.get_object_from_name(n); return {f:round(float(s.get(o,f)),3) for f in ['x','y','theta','store_full','calibrated','at_home']}
           6 +def F(s,n):
           7 +    o=s.get_object_from_name(n); return {f:round(float(s.get(o,f)),3) for f in o.type.__dict__.get('features',[])} 
           8 +def dump(s):
           9 +    for n in sorted(s.get_object_names()):
          10 +        o=s.get_object_from_name(n)
          11 +        print(n, o.type.name, s.vec([o]).round(3).tolist())
          12 +class Sim:
          13 +    def __init__(s,seed=0):
          14 +        s.env=make_env(); s.obs,_=s.env.reset(seed=seed)
          15 +    def act(s,a0=(0,0,0,'noop'),a1=(0,0,0,'noop')):
          16 +        a=[a0[0],a0[1],a0[2],SEL[a0[3]],a1[0],a1[1],a1[2],SEL[a1[3]]]
          17 +        s.obs,r,te,tr,info=s.env.step(np.array(a,dtype=np.float32)); return r,te
          18 +    def r(s,i): return R(s.obs,'rover%d'%i)
          19 +    def goto(s,i,x,y,th=None,maxit=200):
          20 +        for _ in range(maxit):
          21 +            c=s.r(i); dx=np.clip(x-c['x'],-.2,.2); dy=np.clip(y-c['y'],-.2,.2)
          22 +            dth=0 if th is None else np.clip((th-c['theta']+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi,-.4,.4)
          23 +            if abs(dx)<1e-3 and abs(dy)<1e-3 and abs(dth)<1e-3: return True
          24 +            a=(dx,dy,dth,'noop'); 
          25 +            p=s.r(i)
          26 +            if i==0: s.act(a0=a)
          27 +            else: s.act(a1=a)
          28 +            if s.r(i)==p: return False
          29 +        return False
          30 +def gp(s,i,pts,th=None):
          31 +    for p in pts:
          32 +        if not s.goto(i,p[0],p[1],th): return False
          33 +    return True
          34 +def objf(s,k,f): return float(s.obs.get(s.obs.get_object_from_name('objective%d'%k),f))
          35 +def prep0(seed=0):
          36 +    s=Sim(seed); s.goto(0,1.0,0.5); s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'cal')); s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'img'))
          37 +    assert objf(s,0,'have_image_rover0')==1
          38 +    return s

diff --git a/pC_lib.py b/pC_lib.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..51351dd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/pC_lib.py
@@ -0,0 +1,24 @@
           1 +import numpy as np
           2 +from env_client import make_env
           3 +SEL=dict(sample=-0.8333,calibrate=-0.5,image=-0.1667,noop=0,send=0.5,drop=0.8333)
           4 +env=make_env()
           5 +class S: obs=None; te=False; tr=False; n=0
           6 +def reset(seed):
           7 +    S.obs,info=env.reset(seed=seed); S.n=0; return info
           8 +def g(name,f): o=S.obs.get_object_from_name(name); return float(S.obs.get(o,f))
           9 +def R(i): return [round(g(f'rover{i}',f),3) for f in ['x','y','theta','store_full','calibrated','at_home']]
          10 +def SM(j): return [round(g(f'sample{j}',f),3) for f in ['x','y','z','is_soil','analyzed_rover0','analyzed_rover1','received_analysis']]
          11 +def step(a0=(0,0,0),s0='noop',a1=(0,0,0),s1='noop'):
          12 +    a=list(a0)+[SEL[s0]]+list(a1)+[SEL[s1]]
          13 +    S.obs,r,te,tr,info=env.step(np.array(a,dtype=np.float32)); S.n+=1
          14 +    S.te,S.tr=te,tr; return r,te,tr
          15 +def goto(i,x,y,th=None,maxn=200):
          16 +    for _ in range(maxn):
          17 +        p=R(i); dx=x-p[0]; dy=y-p[1]; dt=0 if th is None else (th-p[2]+np.pi)%(2*np.pi)-np.pi
          18 +        if abs(dx)<1e-3 and abs(dy)<1e-3 and abs(dt)<1e-3: return True
          19 +        m=(np.clip(dx,-.2,.2),np.clip(dy,-.2,.2),np.clip(dt,-.2,.2))
          20 +        if i==0: step(m)
          21 +        else: step(a1=m)
          22 +        q=R(i)
          23 +        if q[:3]==p[:3]: print('stuck',i,p); return False
          24 +    return False

           1 +import numpy as np
           2 +from pB_lib import Sim, objf, gp
           3 +SEED=44
           4 +def prep(s0):
           5 +    s=Sim(SEED)
           6 +    assert gp(s,0,[(1.0,0.7)]),'r0 path'
           7 +    s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'cal')); s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'img'))
           8 +    k=[k for k in range(3) if objf(s,k,'have_image_rover0')==1]
           9 +    assert k,'noimg'
          10 +    s.k=k[0]
          11 +    assert gp(s,0,[(s0[0],s0[1])],th=s0[2]),'r0 to S'
          12 +    return s
          13 +def place1(s,p):
          14 +    # move rover1 to p: go via y=-0.3 corridor first
          15 +    pts=[(-1.0,-0.6),(p[0],-0.6),(p[0],p[1])] if p[1]>-1.4 or True else [(p[0],p[1])]
          16 +    s.goto(1,-1.0,-0.6); s.goto(1,p[0],max(p[1],-0.6) if p[1]>-0.6 else -0.6)
          17 +    ok=s.goto(1,p[0],p[1],th=p[2])
          18 +    r=s.r(1); return ok and abs(r['x']-p[0])<1e-3 and abs(r['y']-p[1])<1e-3
          19 +def send(s):
          20 +    s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'send'))
          21 +    return objf(s,s.k,'received_image')==1
          22 +def trial(args):
          23 +    s0,p=args
          24 +    s=prep(s0)
          25 +    if p is not None:
          26 +        if not place1(s,p): return None
          27 +    else: s.goto(1,-1.0,-0.3)
          28 +    return send(s)
          29 +def sensept(s0):
          30 +    x,y,th=s0; c,sn=np.cos(th),np.sin(th)
          31 +    return np.array([x+c*-0.087-sn*-0.012, y+sn*-0.087+c*-0.012])
          32 +L=np.array([-1.9,-2.0])
          33 +def pos_on_line(s0,t,off,th=0.0):
          34 +    a=sensept(s0); d=L-a; n=np.linalg.norm(d); u=d/n; perp=np.array([-u[1],u[0]])
          35 +    q=a+t*d+off*perp; return (float(q[0]),float(q[1]),th)

           1 +import sys
           2 +from multiprocessing import Pool
           3 +from pD_lib import *
           4 +def bis(job):
           5 +    S,t,side,th=job
           6 +    lo,hi=0.0,0.5  # lo blocked, hi free
           7 +    if trial((S,pos_on_line(S,t,side*hi,th))) is not True: return job,'hi not free'
           8 +    for _ in range(8):
           9 +        m=(lo+hi)/2; r=trial((S,pos_on_line(S,t,side*m,th)))
          10 +        if r is None: return job,('placefail',m)
          11 +        if r: hi=m
          12 +        else: lo=m
          13 +    return job,(round(lo,4),round(hi,4))

          15 +    S=(0.4,-0.6,np.pi)
          16 +    jobs=[(S,t,sd,th) for t in [0.35,0.5,0.65,0.72] for sd in [1,-1] for th in [0.0,np.pi/4]]
          17 +    with Pool(8) as p:
          18 +        for j,r in p.imap(bis,jobs): print('t=%.2f side=%+d th=%.2f'%j[1:],r,flush=True)

           1 +import json, sys

           3 +from env_client import make_env
           4 +def get(seed):
           5 +    env=make_env(); obs,info=env.reset(seed=seed)
           6 +    out={'info':info,'objs':{}}

          11 +    env.close(); return seed,out

           1 +import json, sys, time
           2 +from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
           3 +class T:
           4 +    def __init__(s,n): s.name=n
           5 +class O:
           6 +    def __init__(s,n,t): s.name=n; s.type=T(t)
           7 +class FakeState:
           8 +    def __init__(s,objs): s.objs=objs; s.o={n:O(n,v['type']) for n,v in objs.items()}
           9 +    def get_object_names(s): return set(s.objs)
          10 +    def get_object_from_name(s,n): return s.o[n]
          11 +    def get(s,o,f): return s.objs[o.name]['f'][f]
          12 +def run(args):
          13 +    seed, st = args
          14 +    import approach
          15 +    ap=approach.GeneratedApproach(None,None,{})
          16 +    t=time.time()
          17 +    ap.reset(FakeState(st['objs']), st['info'])
          18 +    tp=time.time()-t
          19 +    from approach import parse
          20 +    d=parse(FakeState(st['objs']))
          21 +    steps=ap._simulate(d)
          22 +    return seed, st['info'].get('object_count'), steps, ap.plan_cost, round(tp,2)
          23 +if __name__=='__main__':
          24 +    S=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
          25 +    lo,hi=int(sys.argv[2]),int(sys.argv[3])
          26 +    items=[(int(k),v) for k,v in S.items() if lo<=int(k)<hi]
          27 +    with ProcessPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
          28 +        res=list(ex.map(run, items))
          29 +    res.sort()
          30 +    if len(sys.argv)>4:
          31 +        for r in res: print(*r)
          32 +    print('TOTAL', sum(r[2] for r in res), 'N', len(res), 'maxt', max(r[4] for r in res))

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f03351f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/pD_scan2.py
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
           1 +import sys, json
           2 +from multiprocessing import Pool
           3 +from pB_lib import *
           4 +from pD_lib import pos_on_line
           5 +IMG={2:(0.4,0.2),1:(1.0,0.3)}
           6 +def image(s,k,S):
           7 +    gp(s,0,[IMG[k]],th=np.pi); s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'cal')); s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'img'))
           8 +    assert objf(s,k,'have_image_rover0')==1 and objf(s,k,'received_image')==0
           9 +    assert gp(s,0,[(S[0],IMG[k][1]),(S[0],S[1])],th=S[2])
          10 +def scanside(s,k,S,t,side,th,offs):
          11 +    out=[]
          12 +    for o in offs:
          13 +        p=pos_on_line(S,t,side*o,th)
          14 +        ok=s.goto(1,p[0],p[1],th=p[2]); r=s.r(1)
          15 +        if not(ok and abs(r['x']-p[0])<2e-3 and abs(r['y']-p[1])<2e-3): out.append((o,None)); continue
          16 +        s.act(a0=(0,0,0,'send'))
          17 +        res=objf(s,k,'received_image')==1; out.append((o,res))
          18 +        if res: break
          19 +    return out
          20 +def job(j):
          21 +    S,t,th=j
          22 +    try:
          23 +        s=Sim(44); s.goto(1,-1.0,-0.3)
          24 +        offs=list(np.round(np.arange(0,0.301,0.01),3))
          25 +        image(s,2,S); a=scanside(s,2,S,t,+1,th,offs)
          26 +        s.goto(1,-1.0,-0.3)
          27 +        image(s,1,S); b=scanside(s,1,S,t,-1,th,offs)
          28 +        return j,a,b
          29 +    except Exception as e: return j,'ERR',repr(e)
          30 +def summ(a):
          31 +    if a=='ERR': return a
          32 +    fails=[o for o,r in a if r is None]; succ=[o for o,r in a if r]
          33 +    blocked=[o for o,r in a if r is False]
          34 +    return 'first_free=%s lastblocked=%s placefail=%s'%(succ[0] if succ else None, blocked[-1] if blocked else None, fails[:3])
          35 +if __name__=='__main__':
          36 +    S=tuple(json.loads(sys.argv[1])); ths=json.loads(sys.argv[2]); ts=json.loads(sys.argv[3])
          37 +    jobs=[(S,t,th) for th in ths for t in ts]
          38 +    with Pool(int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv)>4 else 8) as p:
          39 +        for j,a,b in p.imap(job,jobs):
          40 +            print('t=%.2f th=%.2f | +side %s | -side %s'%(j[1],j[2],summ(a),summ(b) if a!='ERR' else b),flush=True)
